_selection_rule: 3-4 test models from different families, one large + one small of the same family, judge from a family that is not tested and fixed for all scoring.
_pricing_note: context = max input+output tokens; in/out = credits per 1M tokens as listed in the Adaption docs on 14 Nov 2026. NOT verified by a live call - run `python -m nis2eval smoke`.
_cutoff_note: Smoke test, 14 Nov 2026 (results/smoke.json). training_cutoff_self_reported is what the model answered when asked; self-reports are unreliable (deepseek-v4-flash said October 2024 in one run and June 2024 in the next). training_cutoff is from a web search on 14 Nov 2026 and only gemma's comes from a model card: three models are dated before the decree, qwen3.8-27b is unknown. Open the vendor model cards before the report quotes any of these. knows_decree is the smoke probe 'what is DL 125/2025': all four said they did not know it, so C0 is read as 'does the model say so'. The decree fits every model: 52-56k input tokens.

_judge_note: History. Planned: glm-5.2 (a family not under test). 14 Nov: glm-5.2 answered 504 all afternoon, so the pilot was graded by deepseek-v4-flash, which is also a test model. 15 Nov 03:47 IST: deepseek-v4-flash started answering HTTP 502 (provider failure). glm-5.2 answered short calls again but refused judge-sized calls with HTTP 429 even with nothing else running (04:20 to 04:27 IST). The full run is therefore graded by the two models that stayed up and cache the decree: qwen3.8-27b (main, scores.csv) and gemma-4-31b-it (second, scores.gemma-4-31b-it.csv). Both are test models; each analysis is also produced without the judge's own answers. The 86 full-run judgments deepseek made before it failed are kept (scores.deepseek-v4-flash.csv).
_fallback_note: The API lists the id as glm-5.3-flash (the docs say glm-53-flash). On 14 Nov 2026 both GLM models answered 504 to most calls, streamed or not.
_output_budget_note: All hosted models reason before answering and reasoning tokens count against max_output_tokens (qwen3.5-397b spent 2,000+ on a one-line question), so the budgets are well above the expected answer length. Check the `incomplete` field of answers.jsonl after each run.
_reasoning_note: The API's default reasoning effort is xhigh (accepted values: xhigh, medium, low, none). At xhigh qwen3.8-27b spent all 12,000 output tokens reasoning and returned no answer in 6 of 9 dry-run calls; at medium it answered in about a minute. One setting for all test models: medium. Note that gemma-4-31b-it did not reason at all when the setting was omitted (dry run) and does reason at medium (pilot: about 600-2,300 reasoning tokens per answer), so for that model medium is more reasoning than its default, not less. The judge also runs at medium: at xhigh glm-5.3-flash spent about 10,000 reasoning tokens on one judgment.
_rate_limit_note: Measured 15 Nov 2026: one limit per account for all keys and models (four keys did not raise it). It follows prompt size: about 15 short calls a minute pass; calls carrying the 50,000-token decree are refused above roughly 3 a minute. The client paces itself by input tokens per minute (NIS2_TPM) and adjusts on HTTP 429. Sixteen short calls at once on four keys were all accepted, so it is not a cap on calls in flight.

second_judge.note: Grades C0, C1, C2 a second time. Also a test model: analyses are also produced without its own answers.

dropped_test_models.note: Tried as a supplementary model on 15 Nov and dropped. At the common settings (reasoning effort 'medium', 12,000 output tokens) it returned no answer in 35 of 53 calls: the budget went on reasoning. With a 32,000 and a 64,000 budget it answered after 16,149 and 45,234 reasoning tokens (102 s and 265 s); at effort 'low' it did not reason at all. Its 18 answers are in answers.jsonl and are not analysed.
